source_text: Μετὰ ταῦτα τὸ περιτέμνεσθαι τὰ αἰδοῖα μὴ διαβαλὼν ὁ Κέλσος ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων γινόμενον, φησὶν ἀπὸ Αἰγυπτίων αὐτὸ ἐληλυθέναι, Αἰγυπτίοις μᾶλλον ἢ Μωϋσεῖ πιστεύσας, λέγοντι πρῶτον ἐν ἀνθρώποις περιτετμῆσθαι τὸν Ἀβραάμ. τοῦ δ᾿ Ἀβραὰμ τὸ ὄνομα οὐ Μωυσῆς ἀναγράφει μόνος οἰκειῶν αὐτὸν θεῷ, ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν ἐπᾳδόντων δαίμονας χρῶνται ἐν τοῖς λόγοις αὐτῶν τῷ „ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ,“ ποιοῦντες μὲν διὰ τὸ ὄνομα καὶ τὴν πρὸς τὸν δίκαιον τοῦ θεοῦ οἰκειότητα, διὸ παραλαμβάνουσι τὴν „(ὁ) θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ“ λέξιν. οὐκ ἐπιστάμενοι δὲ, τίς ἐστιν ὁ Ἀβραάμ. τὰ δ᾿ αὐτὰ λεκτέον καὶ περὶ τοῦ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περὶ τοῦ Ἰακὼβ καὶ περὶ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ· ἅτινα ὁμολογουμένως Ἑβραῖα ὄντα ὀνόματα πολλαχοῦ τοῖς Αἰγυπτίοις ἐπαγγελλομένοις ἐνέργειάν τινα ἐνέσπαρται μαθήμασι. τὸν δὲ λόγον τῆς περιτομῆς, ἀρξάμενον ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ κωλυόμενον ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, μὴ βουλομένου τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ μαθητὰς τὸ αὐτὸ ποιεῖν. οὐ πρόκειται νῦν ἑρμηνεύειν. οὐ γὰρ τῆς περὶ τούτων διδασκαλίας ὁ παρὼν καιρὸς ἀλλ᾿ ἀγῶνος καθαιροῦντος τὰ φερόμενα ὑπὸ Κέλσου κατὰ τοῦ Ἰουδαίων λόγου ἐγκλήματα, οἰομένου τάχιον ψευδοποιήσειν τὸν χριστιανισμὸν, ἐὰν τῆς ἀρχῆς αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαϊκοῖς οὔσης λόγοις κατηγορῶν παραστήσῃ κἀκεῖνον ψευδῆ.
pass_a_gloss: After these things, Celsus, not having spoken against the circumcision of the private parts as being done by Jews, says it came from Egyptians, having trusted Egyptians more than Moses, saying that Abraham was the first among men to be circumcised. Now, Moses alone does not write the name of Abraham as being one who is owned by God, but also many of those who conjure up demons use the phrase 'the God of Abraham' in their speeches, doing this because of the name and the relationship to the righteous God, therefore they take up the phrase 'the God of Abraham'. Not knowing, however, who Abraham is. The same things must be said also concerning Isaac and concerning Jacob and concerning Israel; which, being confessedly Hebrew names, are sprinkled in many places among the teachings of the Egyptians who promise some kind of efficacy. The account of circumcision, having begun from Abraham and being forbidden by Jesus, not wanting his disciples to do the same thing. It is not the time now to interpret. For the present time is not for the teaching concerning these things, but for removing the accusations brought by Celsus against the Jewish speech, thinking that he will more quickly falsify Christianity, if, its origin being in Jewish speeches, he presents accusations and also shows that one to be false.
pass_b_english: After this, Celsus does not attack circumcision as a Jewish practice; instead he claims it originated with the Egyptians, trusting Egyptian testimony over Moses, who says Abraham was the first man to be circumcised. It is not Moses alone who records Abraham's name as belonging to God; many who conjure demons also invoke the phrase "the God of Abraham" in their incantations. They do this because of the name itself and the implied kinship between God and the righteous one, so they adopt the formula "the God of Abraham" even though they do not actually know who Abraham is. The same must be said of Isaac, Jacob, and Israel; these admittedly Hebrew names are scattered throughout Egyptian magical texts that promise some kind of power. The history of circumcision, which begins with Abraham and is prohibited by Jesus because he does not want his disciples to practice it, is not for interpretation now. The present moment is not for teaching on these matters but for dismantling the charges Celsus brings against the Jewish narrative, since he thinks he can more quickly disprove Christianity if he can show its Jewish origins to be false.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex sentence regarding the use of the phrase 'the God of Abraham' by demon-conjurers and the distinction between Moses's usage and that of the magicians. The translation of 'ἐπαγγελλομένοις ἐνέργειάν τινα' as 'promise some kind of efficacy' (A) and 'promise some kind of power' (B) is faithful to the sense of efficacy/power in a magical context. The distinction between the purpose of the current discourse (refuting Celsus) and the actual teaching on circumcision is preserved.
